unit_of_sale: per seat per month, annual or multi-year contracts
products_or_lanes: Pro: Core + payments and ERP sync
cost_estimates_note: All cost numbers are illustrative estimates. Hosting $6 given by seller as illustrative; Pro pass-through $4/seat/mo and $120/hr onboarding are interviewer defaults accepted by the seller.
margin_basis: gross_margin (price = cost / (1 - margin)); the current engine uses markup (cost x (1 + margin)) and needs an extension

levers.hint_text: A year-long or longer commitment improves pricing.
Paying faster, such as annually upfront, improves pricing.
levers.seller_wording: Pay annually upfront (~3 points); approximated by NET15 until a native upfront-billing lever exists

levers.hint_text: Slower payment terms increase the price.
Committing to more seats improves pricing.
levers.seller_wording: Not used as-is: hardcoded threshold (30 loads/week) does not fit seat commitments; credit 0

levers.hint_text: Scheduling flexibility does not change pricing.
Committing to more seats improves pricing.
Partnering with us on a customer story improves pricing.

levers.seller_wording: Native annual-upfront billing lever to replace the NET15 proxy

agent_persona: You are the sales desk of Lumen Ledger, an AP-automation software company serving mid-market finance teams. You negotiate per-seat subscription contracts for Core (invoice capture and approvals) and Pro (adds payments and ERP sync) with buyers, usually their AI procurement agents. You are crisp and consultative: you clarify seat count, product, term and billing, steer buyers toward longer commitments, upfront payment, larger seat commitments and case-study partnerships rather than straight discounts, and you never state a price that did not come from a tool.

proposed_pricing_model.cost_per_seat_month: hosting_per_seat_month + (product=PRO ? passthrough_per_seat_month : 0) + (new_logo ? onboarding_hours x onboarding_rate / (seats x term_months) : 0)
proposed_pricing_model.worked_example: Core, 100 seats, 12 months, new logo, STANDARD: cost = 6 + 2400/1200 = $8.00; list = 8/0.20 = $40.00; floor with no levers = 8/0.35 = $22.86
